title: Race information — official international registration page (fees, fundraising, aid, medical, wildlife safety)
publisher: Lewa Safari Marathon (official event site, Tusk and Lewa Wildlife Conservancy)
claims: International entry for full and half marathon is GBP 150, with a minimum fundraising requirement of GBP 1,750 per person; kids' 5 km entry is GBP 50 and spectator entry GBP 150; no fundraising minimum applies to kids or spectators.
Age categories: full and half marathon open to entrants aged 18 and over; junior categories cover ages 10–13 and 14–17.
Water stations are placed every 2.5 km, offering water, energy drink, oranges and bananas, with food at the finish and misting stations on course.

Medical cover: first aid every 2.5 km with a Red Cross member at each water station; helicopter on standby to the AMREF tent at the finish; equipped planes on standby for evacuation to Nairobi; a recovery staffed by doctors, medics and physios; a Red Cross ambulance at the finish plus three ambulances around the course.

An AMREF Maisha Bronze month subscription is included (26 June – 9 July) and covers up to two air evacuations within Kenya annually; this is not medical insurance, only an air ambulance evacuation cover, and all runners must hold full medical insurance; the event is not liable for medical costs beyond air evacuation.

Wildlife safety: runners must stay on the designated course and use official toilets only; the course is patrolled at all times by armed rangers, and a helicopter plus Supercub light aircraft monitor large species.
Downloadable documents listed on the page include the race rules, course route map, site map and terrain profile; GPX availability is not stated on the page.
